messages.subject: Internal mass cal
parts:
Hi,

I am looking to apply internal mass calibration to data in imzML format. I was hoping that this was possible with the new mzAlign function, but I get the feeling the reference has to include all features rather than select calibrant ions. Is there a function that allows internal mass cal or can mzAlign be easily extended?

Best wishes,
Matt

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Internal mass cal
parts:
Hi Matt,

The reference for mzAlign() does not need to include all features. A few calibrant ions is fine.

The more reference points, the better, however, and they should span most of the relevant mass range. Each entire spectrum will be warped based on whatever references you provide.

I will note, though, that this feature is still relatively experimental and untested, as I haven't had access to an appropriate dataset on which to test and evaluate it. I know at least one other user has had some useful experience with it.

I look forward to any feedback you may have if/when you try it.

-Kylie

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Internal mass cal
parts:
Thanks for reminding me this is not as simple as it should be.

Currently, mzAlign() expects a well-aligned reference spectrum (given as the parameter ref) that shares the same m/z-values as the unaligned spectra--i.e., same m/z as mz(obj). This reference spectrum is just a vector of intensities. The only thing that matters is it should have peaks in the correct places (for the calibrants).

The method then works by shifting the intensities in the unaligned spectra toward the most intense peaks (top x% specified as by quantile) in the reference spectrum. For this to work well, the most intense peaks in the reference spectrum should be calibrant ions that appear across all (or most) of the unaligned spectra.

If you happen to have such a reference spectrum with peaks where the calibrant ions should be--and where the m/z values match the m/z values in the unaligned spectra--then you can just provide this vector of intensities. If you don't, then it's a little more complicated, and you'll have to create a synthetic spectrum. This is the part that should be easier than it currently is.

If you need to create a synthetic reference spectrum, you could either do so either by using simulateSpectrum() or just creating a vector of zeroes as long as your unaligned spectra and inserting nonzero intensities where the calibrant ions should be.

This is an extra step that shouldn't be necessary (if you don't have a full reference spectrum), as--theoretically--you should only need to provide a list of m/z-values where the calibrants should appear, but for some reason I didn't implement it that way. I'll put that on my TODO list.

-Kylie

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Internal mass cal
parts:
Yes, simulateSpectrum() provides a list of both m/z values and intensities. You just need the vector of intensities, so access them via obj$intensity. Note that you need to simulate the spectrum such that the m/z-values are the same as the original (uncalibrated) spectra. Again, this is more complicated than it needs to be, so simplifying this process will be put on my TODO list.

Whether you do it this way or the vector of 0s and 1s, I suggest setting the quantile parameter close to 1 (exactly 1 if the latter), as the only peaks are the calibrant peaks.

The method works by keeping the same m/z-values and warping the shape of the spectrum itself, so the intensities (and peak locations) shift onto the m/z-values where they should be located. So the output spectra will have the same m/z range (and values), but with the peaks shifted.

-Kylie
